commits.messageBody:
Retain the Win32 assembly and use explicit SSE operations, CPUID and prefetch intrinsics on x64. Preserve arithmetic grouping, discarded-lane evaluation and sequential alias behavior; no feature or math path is replaced with a no-op.

Native v120 Debug/Release comparisons expose a pre-existing Win32 register-clobber bug between asm blocks. Disassembly and a tiny six-build discriminator confirm it. A separately named diagnostic reload control (not stock) agrees with x64 on finite/subnormal/extreme/discarded-lane cases in a 33,280-record corpus; exceptional NaN differences remain. No callers of the four arithmetic helpers were found in the client tree; this is not gameplay acceptance or a general bit-identity claim.

(cherry picked from commit ad4d5c7f814f5d4b061fb738f3046253d538bf53)
commits.messageHeadline: math: provide x64 SSE intrinsics for legacy Windows helpers

commits.messageBody:
Retain Win32 assembly; on x64 preserve its add grouping, zero-lane additions and read-before-write alias contract using unaligned SSE loads.

Actual client translation-unit probes under v120 Debug/Release record 1,024 cases each. Stock and candidate Win32 records match. All 768 finite records, tested aliases and control checks match x64; Debug is exact throughout. Release has 464 NaN-payload word differences in 136 exceptional records, retained as an explicit limit. Normal client dispatch and scene acceptance remain untested.

(cherry picked from commit 1cc02f6ab4fce25e26ca7c04da1ae4813fd3f0a1)

Replace only the unavailable x64 FSQRT assembly path with SQRTSS on the already-rounded float input. Win32 assembly and other platform paths stay unchanged.

Matching client sharedCollision builds all four v120 configurations. Actual normalization/line-twist probes match all 8,192 sampled values, classifications and MXCSR records per Debug/Release run against PC64 Win32; candidate Win32 records are unchanged. Separate x87 status words differ by design and remain recorded. No exhaustive numerical or gameplay equivalence claim.
